syllabus_topics: Time-guided systems. Models of economic, physical, electromechanical, electronic, energy, cellular biology, population dynamics systems, etc.
Linear and non-linear dynamic state models.
Numerical solution of systems of equations and ordinary and partial differential equations.
Monte Carlo method. Examples: manufacturing systems, computer networks, communications.
Agent-based modeling and simulation. Examples: Biological systems, autonomous vehicles, air traffic.
assessment_rules: The final grade is the closest integer to (L+E)/2. An additional condition for approval is that the closest integer to E must be greater than or equal to 8. The special examination period follows the same method, requiring both laboratory and exam components. Any fraud or attempt at fraud detected during an assessment or proven by subsequent evidence will result in the annulment of the assessments of all students involved.
bibliography: Cassandras, C.G., Lafortune, Introduction to Discrete Event Systems, The Kluwer International Serie, Academic Publishers, 1999 (main)
